rules.rule: Accelerator detectors, topology probing, and health checks. Every module must start with `from __future__ import annotations as __future_annotations__`. Detectors must degrade to an empty result and log at debug level on hosts without that vendor rather than raising. A new detector must be registered in gpustack_runtime/detector/__init__.py. Verify ctypes/vendor library calls and error handling against the matching py* binding (do not review py*/** internals, which are excluded). Flag shared mutable state or caching bugs, physical-vs-logical device index confusion, and missing or stale Google-style docstrings on public APIs. A behavior change or bug fix requires focused sample-based tests under tests/gpustack_runtime/detector/ that do not require real hardware. State this as a reminder only — tests/ is excluded from this review, so never claim a test is present or absent, and never infer absence from not having seen it.

Container runtime deployers (Docker, Kubernetes, Podman), CDI generators, hostfs inspection, and mirrored deployment. Every module must start with `from __future__ import annotations as __future_annotations__`. Deployers must raise OperationError or UnsupportedError from gpustack_runtime/deployer/__types__.py rather than leaking runtime-client exceptions through the public API. A new deployer must be registered in gpustack_runtime/deployer/__init__.py. Treat host-path binds, hostfs symlink resolution, privileged/capability escalation, secret or sensitive environment variable logging, and mirrored deployment exclusions (never mirroring docker.sock, podman.sock, or the configured host root such as /host) as security-sensitive. Flag duplicate mount targets, partial-failure resource leaks, and unsafe shared state. A behavior change or bug fix requires focused mocked-client tests under tests/gpustack_runtime/deployer/ without requiring a live container runtime. State this as a reminder only — tests/ is excluded from this review, so never claim a test is present or absent, and never infer absence from not having seen it.

CLI subcommands under the gpustack-runtime entrypoint. Every module must start with `from __future__ import annotations as __future_annotations__`. Flag unhandled runtime exceptions leaking raw tracebacks where explicit error messages and exit codes are expected, unsafe argument handling, or breaking changes to CLI flags and structured output formats.

Environment variable registry. Flag any mismatch in name, type, default value, or parsing semantics between the TYPE_CHECKING declarations and the runtime variables mapping. Require Google-style docstrings on new or changed variables since they render into the published API reference.

Deployment manifests. Flag invalid resource names, selectors, probes, RBAC permissions, overly broad privileges or host mounts, secrets exposed in plain text, or configuration that diverges from gpustack_runtime.

Container image build definitions and scripts. Flag leaked build secrets or tokens, broken multi-arch build assumptions, unsafe shell scripting, or mismatches with pyproject.toml and runtime entrypoints.
Canonical repository README. Flag credentials or other secrets in examples, and documentation that contradicts the CLI, environment variables, or shipped library behavior.

MkDocs configuration. Pages omitted from nav are still built and published, but are excluded from global navigation and previous/next links; check whether a new page under docs/ is intended to be discoverable in nav rather than claiming it is unpublished. Flag navigation entries that point to a missing page or conflict with the documentation structure.
